name: Rajagala Monastery, Uhana (archaeological)
description: Rajagala Monastery, located in Uhana within the Ampara district, is an archaeological site featuring ancient cave monasteries. The monastery, believed to date back to the 3rd century BCE, was likely founded by Buddhist monks seeking solitude and tranquility. Visitors can explore the well-preserved caves, some still containing ancient frescoes, and enjoy breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape. Meditation benches have been placed for those seeking inner peace amidst nature's beauty. The site also offers insights into early Sri Lankan architectural and religious practices.
activities: Explore ancient ruins, take in panoramic views, meditate in caves

name: Deegavapi Raja Maha Viharaya (Solosmasthana stupa)
description: Deegavapi Raja Maha Viharaya, also known as Solosmasthana stupa, is a sacred Buddhist site in Ampara District, Sri Lanka. The exact age of the stupa is unknown, but it holds significant historical and religious importance. Legend has it that King Dutugemunu, a prominent figure in Sri Lankan history, constructed it around the 3rd century BCE. Visitors can explore the tranquil surroundings and learn about the stupa's rich heritage, while taking photos of this ancient monument that continues to attract pilgrims and tourists alike.
activities: Explore the serene surroundings, Learn about the site's history, Take photos of the stupa

name: Kudumbigala Monastery (ancient cave monastery)
description: Discover Kudumbigala Monastery, an ancient Buddhist cave complex carved into the rock by skilled artisans over centuries. Explore its serene chambers, each telling tales of faith and craftsmanship that have stood the test of time.
activities: Explore the ancient caves, Learn about Buddhist history, Take in the stunning views
